A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Q♯ research work. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original star-graph experiments, GSM8K and MATH evaluations, component ablations, and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds longer-path star-graph, Qwen, AIME-24, QuALITY, PPO-guidance, and runtime results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same distributional learning, aggregated rollout collection, and reference-policy guidance procedures. The Q-type/V-type implementations and top-20-token inference approach also remain. Applying Q♯ to Qwen or a PPO-trained reference does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds AIME-24 competition mathematics, QuALITY long-passage multiple-choice reading comprehension, and the longer-path G(2,20) star-graph scenario. These substantially broaden evaluation beyond v1's retained GSM8K, MATH, and shorter star graphs.

E2.justification: Table 7 newly evaluates PPO and PPO+Q♯ on MATH; PPO was previously discussed but not experimentally compared there. Existing CD/reference comparisons and the star-graph REINFORCE, DPO, RPO, and CD baselines remain.

E3.justification: Existing splits, accuracy metrics, sampling settings, and training defaults are retained. Added experiments introduce Qwen 2.5 7B references with 1.5B guidance for mathematics, comparisons of base/PPO policies with and without guidance, and timed MATH inference on an A6000. These are additional configurations and procedures, not documented revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: The prefix, parameterization, loss, iteration, and η analyses and qualitative examples are retained. v2 adds focused investigations of longer-horizon shortcut robustness in Figure 2, compatibility with PPO in Appendix I, and computational overhead in Appendix J.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice; theoretical variance bounds do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 5–7, the G(2,20) plot, and runtime measurements. For example, AIME-24 pass@1 is 9.3/13.5/14.1 for reference/CD/Q♯, while MATH pass@1 is 68.4 for PPO and 71.1 for PPO+Q♯. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance changes between versions under retained settings.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorem statements, bounds, and supporting lemmas are largely retained. However, the Theorem 4.4 proof changes a subtracted optimal-policy Q term to a current-policy Q term in its first equality, while the following equality still uses the optimal-policy term (v1 Appendix A; v2 Appendix B). This introduces a localized mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introduction contributions retain the same claims: principled KL-regularized guidance, realizability-based variance-dependent guarantees, correction of star-graph shortcuts, and improved mathematical reasoning with lower KL. The additional evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the shortcut mechanism explanation through sparse-parity and gradient-learning arguments, and explicitly discusses stochastic-transition limitations in Section 5. It adds interpretations concerning model-family generalization, PPO complementarity, generation diversity, and runtime overhead. Conversely, v1's discussion of majority voting's limitations for proof-based questions is omitted.

D1.justification: Appendices I–J newly document training resources and times, A6000 inference timing, and implementation using Hugging Face LogitProcessor and key-value caches. Existing data-collection settings, optimizer hyperparameters, top-20-token masking, and the public code link remain. These additions primarily disclose technical information rather than establish changes to existing implementations.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating related work to Appendix A, v2 adds substantive comparisons with DPO's sequence-level formulation, stable distributional-RL losses, and DualDICE/AlgaeDICE density-ratio approaches. It also expands sparse-parity research connections and adds Qwen and QuALITY references. These broaden research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed, with additional comparison headings. Related work moves from Section 5 to Appendix A, the conclusion becomes Limitations & Conclusion, and the appendices are reorganized around the expanded experiments.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS layout substantially repacks the document: algorithms sit beside prose, Tables 3–4 appear side by side, and the tree example becomes Figure 4. Figure 2 gains G(2,20), Tables 5–7 are added, and existing figures and examples are resized or relocated. A long equation in Lemma B.2 now extends beyond the right page edge.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the additional model-family and reading-comprehension evaluations, PPO composition study, and measured computational costs provide useful support for Q♯'s portability and practical value. The explicit stochastic-transition limitation also improves scope clarity. The net gain is limited by sparse protocols for new experiments, continued absence of empirical uncertainty estimates, and the newly inconsistent term in the main proof.
